title: How to invest in bond ladders for predictable returns
description: Building a DIY annuity using Treasuries or Corporate Bonds.
content:
When you buy a 'Bond Fund' (ETF), the share price fluctuates. If interest rates rise, the fund value drops. For investors who need absolute certainty—like knowing exactly how much cash they will have in 3 years for a house—bond funds are too risky. The solution is individual **Bond Laddering**. By buying specific bonds that mature at staggered intervals (e.g., 2026, 2027, 2028), you eliminate market risk. You hold the bond until it matures, getting 100% of your principal back plus interest, regardless of what the market does.

Key Takeaways

  • Principal Protection: Unlike a bond fund, an individual bond has a maturity date. If you hold to maturity, you are guaranteed your money back (barring default). You ignore daily price swings.
  • Cash Flow Engineering: You can structure a ladder to pay out cash exactly when you need it (e.g., tuition payments every September).
  • Yield Curve Optimization: A ladder captures the high yields of longer-term bonds while maintaining the liquidity of shorter-term bonds.
  • Defined Income: You know exactly what your 'paycheck' (coupon payment) will be for the next 10 years.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The US Treasury market is the most liquid in the world. Building a 'Treasury Ladder' is the safest investment strategy in existence. For higher yields, investors can build 'Corporate Ladders' using Investment Grade bonds (Apple, Microsoft, etc.).

Anatomy of a Ladder

Let's say you have $50,000 and want income + safety.

The Setup (The Rungs)

You buy 5 bonds, $10,000 each.

  • Bond A: Matures in 1 Year. Yield 5.0%.
  • Bond B: Matures in 2 Years. Yield 4.8%.
  • Bond C: Matures in 3 Years. Yield 4.6%.
  • Bond D: Matures in 4 Years. Yield 4.5%.
  • Bond E: Matures in 5 Years. Yield 4.5%.

The Rolling Process

Year 1 Ends: Bond A matures. You get your $10,000 back.
Action: You take that $10,000 and buy a new 5-Year Bond (Bond F) for the back of the ladder.
Result: You maintain a constant 5-year average duration, constantly capturing long-term rates while having cash available every single year.

How to Build It at a Brokerage

  1. Log In: Go to Fidelity or Schwab. Select 'Fixed Income' -> 'Search'.
  2. Filter: Select 'US Treasury' or 'Corporate A-Rated'. Choose 'Ask Yield' to sort.
  3. Select Maturities: Pick one bond maturing in Dec 2026, one in Dec 2027, etc.
  4. Check the 'Ask Price': Try to buy near 'Par' (100). If you pay 110, you are paying a premium and will lose capital at maturity. If you pay 95, you get a discount bonus.
  5. Auto-Roll: For Treasuries, enable Auto-Roll if you want it to be passive. For Corporates, you usually have to manually buy the next rung.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this better than a CD ladder?

Treasuries are State Tax Free. CDs are not. If you live in CA/NY, a Treasury ladder usually wins. If you live in TX/FL, compare the raw yields. Corporates pay more but have default risk.

Why not just buy BND?

BND has no maturity date. If rates spike, BND drops 10% and you lose money if you sell. With a ladder, if rates spike, you just wait for maturity and get 100% of your money back. It removes price risk.

What is the minimum?

Usually $1,000 per bond. To build a 5-year ladder, you need $5,000.
